Summary of Changes
------------------

**Major Changes:**
* docs/clustermesh: overhaul Cluster Mesh documentation with a new introduction, improved load-balancing guidance, and Helm-first setup and certificate configuration instructions (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47615, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47351, @MrFreezeex)

**Minor Changes:**
* envoy: demote stale ADS endpoint warning (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47148, @nezdolik)
* Speed up recovery time for disrupted TCP connections that access a DSR-enabled Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47529, @julianwiedmann)

**Bugfixes:**
* azure: Stop issuing redundant CiliumNode status updates on every IPAM sync when the node's Azure interfaces are unchanged. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47449, @jaredledvina)
* bpf: dsr: don't look for TCP header on fragmented packets (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47640, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: hostfw: tolerate unknown CT protocols and rely on policies (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47621, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47343, @smagnani96)
* clustermesh: fix MCS-API CRD install/upgrade when clustermesh-apiserver is started before the CRD version is actually installed (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47824, @MrFreezeex)
* datapath: turn ARP off on the base devices before bringing them up (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47838, @aanm)
* endpoint/watchdog: Avoid warning about endpoints being deleted (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47625, @christarazi)
* endpoint: Fix silent CIDR policy bypass and traffic drops after agent restart (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47880, @weizhoublue)
* envoy.httpUpstreamLingerTimeout accepts `0` as a chart value and templates into configmap. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47741, @jdw6359)
* envoy: restore http-idle-timeout as the route idle timeout source (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47583, @aanm)
* Fix a BPF verifier reject on pre-v5.12 kernels, when IPv6 is enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47765, @julianwiedmann)
* Fix a deadlock in the shutdown of Cilium operator related to CiliumEndpointSlices. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47967, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47802, @bimmlerd)
* Fix a NetworkPolicy update being ignored for up to two minutes when it arrived while an endpoint was waiting for its security identity to be resolved after a pod relabel. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47727, @aanm)
* Fix a spurious "unable to find ifindex for interface MAC" agent warning on EKS ENI IPAM by waiting for the ENI netlink interface before configuring ingress routes and rules. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47295, @aanm)
* Fix abnormal ip allocation caused by hostnetwork pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47552, @haozhangami)
* Fix unintended RevDNAT for client-to-pod TCP connections, when an identical connection was previously established through a DSR Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47593, @julianwiedmann)
* fix: allow setting endpointPolicyUpdateTimeoutDuration in helm (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47754, @weizhoublue)
* Fixed an issue where an HTTPRoute referencing a Gateway with mixed listener protocols (e.g. HTTP and TCP) was incorrectly rejected with `NotAllowedByListeners` when the TCP listener had an explicit `AllowedRoutes.Kinds` restriction. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46842, @pidreher)
* gateway-api/gamma: refresh CEC owner refs on route recreation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47840, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: mark unresolved backend service ports in route status (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47766, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: preserve duplicate HTTPRoute rule precedence (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46696, @thorn3r)
* gateway-api: prevent conflicted listeners from reaching ingestion (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47457, @asauber)
* gateway-api: requeue L4/TLS routes on ServiceImport updates (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47702, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: sync ListenerSet TLS secrets on ListenerSet events (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47627, @mhofstetter)
* ipcache: fix CIDR reference counter to use canonical prefixes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47208, @iwanhae)
* l2announcer: re-evaluate services on frontend changes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47579, @mhofstetter)
* Log the correct route kind when the Gateway API operator fails to list TLSRoutes for a backend Service (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47826, @mehrdadbn9)
* operator: Emit startup logs in the configured log format (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47890, @HadrienPatte)
* Resolve a endpoint manager crash for restored endpoints with verbose policy logging enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47844, @bimmlerd)
* standalone-dns-proxy: return an error when no endpoint is found (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47791, @vipul-21)
* wireguard: Unsubscribe node handler on shutdown (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47614, @HadrienPatte)

* gha/kubespray: run on schedule, rather than on every push (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47719, @giorio94)
* gha/lvh-kind: respect Kind image version also when config is provided (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47703, @giorio94)
* gha: don't install LLVM and Clang in integration tests workflow (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47717, @giorio94)
* gha: fix checkout of trusted branch in smoke and k8s-kind workflows (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47724, @giorio94)
* images/scripts: Validate Envoy image vars against sed injection (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47205, @MasloMaslane)
* Revert "gha: don't install LLVM and Clang in integration tests workflow" (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47780, @giorio94)
* test(bpf): parallelize eBPF test compilation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47426, @lconnery)
* test/cyclonus: log the JUnit XML instead of copying it from a dead pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47725, @aanm)

**Misc Changes:**
* Added documentation for running Cilium in CNI chaining mode on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) with VCN-Native Pod Networking. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46116, @amaanx86)

* bpf: conntrack: Reduce stack usage of `ct_create{4,6}` (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47582, @dylandreimerink)

signals.title: CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy does not allow us to define policy to lockdown traffic within each of the namespaces
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues ### What happened? As of now, if we need to lock down both ingress and egress within a particular namespace, it is achievable only by defining a network policy like the one below. It has to be created for each namespace in the cluster. ``` apiVersion: cilium.io/v2 kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy metadata: name: allow-ns-traffic namespace: default spec: endpointSelector: {} ingress: - fromEndpoints: - {} egress: - toEndpoints: - {} ``` There is no facility to define one cluster-wide policy which automatically enforces this policy for all the namespaces in the cluster including any new namespaces that will be created in the cluster. This is because of the fact there is no possibility to mention the namespace as self. ### Cilium Version 1.30.0 ### Kernel Version 5.15.0-1022-azure ### Kubernetes Version 1.25.2 ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output _No response_ ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Code of Conduct - [X] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: CFP: Correlate policy verdicts to host firewall network policies too
signals.text: ## Cilium Feature Proposal Desired Feature There is a feature to correlate traffic in flows to related policies: #26438 It seems working except for host firewall traffic, which would be nice also if need to debug something related to node or pods with hostnetwork firewalls. Example output for a flow, trying to ssh to a node from external, which is allowed with a ccnp policy (we testing lot of other things so policies in audit mode, but I guess that doesn't change if it shows policy identifications): ``` > hubble observe -f -t policy-verdict --port 22 -o json | jq { "flow": { "time": "2024-07-17T12:36:48.479752205Z", "uuid": "6662257a-4526-4d72-9b4d-7d480f65b2f5", "verdict": "FORWARDED", "ethernet": { "source": "04:8c:16:f3:7d:f0", "destination": "00:50:56:96:93:80" }, "IP": { "source": "10.211.59.133", "destination": "10.211.60.1", "ipVersion": "IPv4" }, "l4": { "TCP": { "source_port": 37304, "destination_port": 22, "flags": { "SYN": true } } }, "source": { "identity": 16777244, "labels": [ "cidr:10.211.59.133/32", "reserved:world" ] }, "destination": { "identity": 1, "labels": [ "reserved:host", "reserved:kube-apiserver" ] }, "Type": "L3_L4", "node_name": "au-cilium-poc/k8smauciliumpoc001", "event_type": { "type": 5 }, "traffic_direction": "INGRESS", "policy_match_type": 2, "is_reply": false, "Summary": "TCP Flags: SYN" }, "node_name": "au-cilium-poc/k8smauciliumpoc001", "time": "2024-07-17T12:36:48.479752205Z" } ``` cilium version 1.15.7 k8s version 1.26.9 os: ubuntu 22.04 Don't know how much host firewall is different in code, so can't give actual proposal. More like a request, that it would be nice if that works with host firewall rules too. Thanks!

signals.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signals.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. When migrating variables, do a quick search through [Paul's macro documentation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/15379#issuecomment-897441189) for a good docstring to use in `DECLARE_CONFIG`. - [ep_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/ep_config.h) - [x] HOST_EP_ID - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [node_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/node_config.h) - [x] CLUSTER_ID - [x] CILIUM_*_IFINDEX, CILIUM_*_MAC (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43474) - [x] TUNNEL_PORT, TUNNEL_PROTOCOL (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43520) - [x] KERNEL_HZ, ENABLE_JIFFIES (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] L2_ANNOUNCEMENTS(_MAX_LIVENESS) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42587) - [x] EPHEMERAL_MIN (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43564) - [x] IS_L3_DEV, NATIVE_DEV_MAC_BY_IFINDEX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/39116 & https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] CLUSTER_ID_MAX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42478) - [x] IDENTITY_{LEN,MAX} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43507) - [x] VTEP_MASK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] NODEPORT_PORT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] IPV4_LOOPBACK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [x] NAT_46X64_PREFIX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43799) - [x] CIDR_IDENTITY_RANGE_{START,END} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44223) - [x] HASH_INIT{4,6}_SEED (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44190) - [x] EVENTS_MAP_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44795) - [ ] VLAN_FILTER (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38721) - [x] Reserved security IDs (HOST_ID, WORLD_ID, ect.) signals.title: Cilium Gateway with Envoy rejects IPv6 PROXY headers from LB while IPv4 works
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.18.4 and lower than v1.19.0 ### What happened? I am using Cilium Gateway API with Envoy for HTTP(S) traffic. The Load Balancer is a Hetzner Cloud LB (TCP mode) with Proxy Protocol enabled. The flow that breaks is as follows: ``` [IPv6 client] -> [Hetzner LoadBalancer] -> (proxy protocol) [IPv4 endpoint on the Kubernetes nodes] ``` With this setup: * IPv4 clients work correctly when Proxy Protocol is enabled. * IPv6 clients fail to connect (connection stalls/handshake never completes). The connection does reach Envoy, as it emits a warning for each IPv6-iniated request: `[21][warning][filter] [cilium/l7policy.cc:100] cilium.l7policy: Cilium policy filter state not found`. When we disable Proxy Protocol on the LB, then both IPv4 and IPv6 work normally. The same Hetzner LB + Proxy Protocol configuration previously worked fine with NGINX Ingress. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Create a Cilium cluster with: ```yaml gatewayAPI: enabled: true enableProxyProtocol: true enableAlpn: true enableAppProtocol: true externalTrafficPolicy: Local ``` 2. Deploy a Gateway + HTTPRoute to an existing service. 3. Attach a Hetzner LB in TCP mode, with PROXY protocol enabled. 4. Send traffic over IPv4 > works. 5. Send traffic over IPv6 > fails (no handshake). 6. Disable Proxy Protocol on the LB → IPv6 works immediately. 7. Re-enable Proxy Protocol > IPv6 fails again. ### Cilium Version v1.18.4 ### Kernel Version 6.12.57-talos ### Kubernetes Version Server Version: v1.34.0 ### Regression Unknown. Just starting to use Gateway API. ### Sysdump It fails to upload. Helm values: ```yaml ipam: mode: kubernetes hubble: relay: enabled: true ui: enabled: true hostFirewall: enabled: false kubeProxyReplacement: true k8s: requireIPv4PodCIDR: true securityContext: capabilities: ciliumAgent: - CHOWN - KILL - NET_ADMIN - NET_RAW - IPC_LOCK - SYS_ADMIN - SYS_RESOURCE - DAC_OVERRIDE - FOWNER - SETGID - SETUID cleanCiliumState: - NET_ADMIN - SYS_ADMIN - SYS_RESOURCE operator: replicas: 2 cgroup: autoMount: enabled: true hostRoot: /sys/fs/cgroup k8sServiceHost: localhost k8sServicePort: "7445" policyAuditMode: false ipv4: enabled: true mtu: 1350 gatewayAPI: enabled: true enableProxyProtocol: true enableAlpn: true enableAppProtocol: true externalTrafficPolicy: Local ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell ❯ openssl s_client -connect "[2a01:4f8:c01e:734::1]:443" -servername microblog.network Connecting to 2a01:4f8:c01e:734::1 CONNECTED(00000003) depth=2 C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1 verify return:1 depth=1 C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R12 verify return:1 depth=0 CN=microblog.network verify return:1 --- Certificate chain 0 s:CN=microblog.network i:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R12 a:PKEY: RSA, 2048 (bit); sigalg: sha256WithRSAEncryption v:NotBefore: Nov 23 06:21:35 2025 GMT; NotAfter: Feb 21 06:21:34 2026 GMT 1 s:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R12 i:C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1 a:PKEY: RSA, 2048 (bit); sigalg: sha256WithRSAEncryption v:NotBefore: Mar 13 00:00:00 2024 GMT; NotAfter: Mar 12 23:59:59 2027 GMT --- Server certificate [snip] subject=CN=microblog.network issuer=C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R12 --- No client certificate CA names sent Peer signing digest: SHA256 Peer signature type: rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 Peer Temp Key: X25519, 253 bits --- SSL handshake has read 3088 bytes and written 1628 bytes Verification: OK --- New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 Protocol: TLSv1.3 Server public key is 2048 bit This TLS version forbids renegotiation. Compression: NONE Expansion: NONE No ALPN negotiated Early data was not sent Verify return code: 0 (ok) # at this point I send the HTTP request: GET / HTTP/1.1 Host: microblog.network Connection: close # it closed the connection: RECONNECTING --- ``` ### Anything else? ^ Relevant log output shows an `openssl` command. Interesting thing here is that its able to reach the cluster, exchanges TLS, verifies the certificate but closes the connection when trying to complete the HTTP request. ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Envoy NPDS not updated when new identities are added for GatewayAPI ingress endpoints doing hairpin traffic for (at least) wildcard matching policies
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.18.5 and lower than v1.19.0 ### What happened? When using Gateway API with L7LB services, hairpin traffic from cluster-internal workloads (e.g., uptime-kuma self-monitoring) to gateway endpoints is intermittently denied by Envoy with "403 Access denied". The issue will crop up sometimes after a cluster-internal workload being monitored is rescheduled. The new backend identity is correctly added to the Cilium agent's policy for the ingress endpoint (visible in `cilium-dbg endpoint get <ingress-endpoint-id>`), but the local Envoy's NPDS is not updated. Envoy denies traffic with: ``` cilium.network: No policy found for id: <identity> ``` **Expected behavior:** When a new identity is added to the selector cache, the ingress endpoint's Envoy NPDS should be updated to include the new identity, allowing traffic to flow. **Actual behavior:** The NPDS remains stale until either: 1. A config change triggers a full policy regeneration on the affected node 2. The cilium-agent pod is restarted 3. A policy change triggers an update of the `reserved:ingress` endpoint and up-to-date identities are pushed. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Deploy Gateway API with HTTPRoutes pointing to backend services on Node A. I'm using Cilium LBIPAM to back the Gateway in this case. 2. Apply a ClusterwideCiliumPolicy that allows traffic from the ingress entity for all relevant workloads that uses an `endpointSelector: {}` selector (so that it ADDITIONALLY matches reserved:ingress). For example a wide-open policy like: ``` spec: egress: - toEntities: - world - remote-node - cluster - kube-apiserver - toEndpoints: - {} endpointSelector: {} ingress: - fromEntities: - world - cluster - remote-node - kube-apiserver - ingress - fromEndpoints: - {} ``` 3. Deploy a monitoring workload (e.g., uptime-kuma) on Node B that performs hairpin requests to services through the gateway's external IP 5. Scale down and up (or delete/recreate) a backend pod that the gateway routes to (e.g. migrate it from Node A to Node C) 6. The new backend pod gets a new identity 7. Hairpin traffic from the monitoring workload to the gateway is denied with 403. In this case I'll see something like the following running when running `cilium-dbg endpoint get [reserved:ingress's identity] |grep revision` on Node A: before restarting the backend: ``` "proxy-policy-revision": 25 "policy-revision": 25 ``` after restarting the backend: ``` "proxy-policy-revision": 25 "policy-revision": 26 ``` and the cilium-agent will have the new identities for the backend workload, but envoy will not have received them. However the issue does not always seem to trigger, probably because of other simultaneous changes that force envoy to be updated with the new identities. But it's often enough to be problematic beyond monitoring (e.g. cert-manager HTTP-01 lets-encrypt challenges' self-check before submission). ### Cilium Version ``` Client: 1.18.5 7d4d8932 2025-12-17T04:56:47+00:00 go version go1.24.11 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.18.5 7d4d8932 2025-12-17T04:56:47+00:00 go version go1.24.11 linux/amd64 ``` But I have been having this issue intermittently since I began using Gateway API circa Cilium 1.16 ### Kernel Version ``` Linux 6.18.1-talos #1 SMP Wed Dec 17 10:07:33 UTC 2025 x86_64 Linux (Talos 1.12.0) ``` ### Kubernetes Version ``` Client Version: v1.35.0 Server Version: v1.35.0 ``` ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? ### Root Cause Analysis Based on code analysis (thanks claude-code plus finally having enough free time to really dig in), the issue appears to be in `/pkg/endpoint/bpf.go` in `applyPolicyMapChangesLocked`: ```go // Line 1093-1094 updateEnvoy := hasNewPolicy // FALSE for incremental identity updates // Line 1115-1128 if !changes.Empty() { // updateEnvoy if there were any mapChanges, but only if the endpoint has Envoy // redirects, or is an Ingress endpoint updateEnvoy = updateEnvoy || hasEnvoyRedirect || e.isIngress } ``` The issue appears to be that `updateEnvoy` is only set to `true` if `!changes.Empty()` is TRUE **first**. For wildcard selectors, it seems no map changes are accumulated because of an early return in `/pkg/policy/l4.go`: ```go // Line 815-816 if cs.IsWildcard() { return // No AccumulateMapChanges called! } ``` The ingress endpoint appears to use wildcard selectors (via `wildcardRule` in `repository.go:463-470`). If this analysis is correct, when new identities are added: 1. `SelectorCache.UpdateIdentities` is called 2. The wildcard selector is notified via `IdentitySelectionUpdated` 3. Early return at line 815-816 because `cs.IsWildcard()` is true 4. No map changes are accumulated 5. In `applyPolicyMapChangesLocked`, `changes.Empty()` returns TRUE 6. `updateEnvoy` is never set despite `e.isIngress` being TRUE 7. `UpdateNetworkPolicy` is never called 8. Envoy NPDS remains stale There may be other factors contributing to this issue that contribute to the issue but haven't yet identified. ### Why this matters for L7LB/Gateway traffic L7LB services like GatewayAPI cause the hairpin traffic to be diverted to the source's **local** Envoy on the source node, which now potentially has stale identities. This means: - Traffic from a monitoring pod on node-A to the gateway IP is redirected to node-A's local Envoy - Node-A's Envoy checks the local ingress endpoint's (reserved:ingress) policy - If the backend's identity is missing from node-A's ingress endpoint NPDS, traffic is denied The ingress endpoint exists on every node with potentially different states if NPDS updates are not triggered. ### Possible Fix Direction If the analysis above is correct, one potential fix might be to modify the condition at line 1115-1128 to trigger Envoy updates for ingress endpoints when there's a new selector snapshot, regardless of whether map changes are empty. However, I don't pretend to understand the cilium architecture well enough; perhaps some other mechanism should also be updating envoy identity data and isn't being triggered in the case of hairpin traffic. ### Workaround Triggering any config change on the affected node's cilium-agent (e.g., toggling debug logging) causes a full policy regeneration which includes calling `UpdateNetworkPolicy` for the ingress endpoint, updating the NPDS with the new identities. ### Cilium Users Document - [x] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Cilium fails to properly write eBPF maps in some circumstances
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.18.8 and lower than v1.19.0 ### What happened? Cilium fails to properly write eBPF maps in some circumstances, seemingly related to Intel ICE drivers(?). This issue has been observed to chronically affect bare metal servers with intel 810 series NICs, but strangely, never any other type of host. It's not known whether ICE plays a factor here, or this is some other strange co-incidence. But this pattern has been observed 1000+ machines for at least a year. ### How can we reproduce the issue? This issue has been reproduced on Cilium 1.18.7, and 1.19.2. on Ubuntu 20.04, and Ubuntu 22.04, with kernels 5.15.0-72 and 6.8.0-101 Install Cilium 1.19.2 on Ubuntu 22.04, with a 6.8.0-101-generic kernel on a bare-metal server with Intel 810 series nic using the latest Intel ICE driver 2.3.15. This does not appear to affect bare metal servers running i40e driver NICs. `modinfo ice filename: /lib/modules/6.8.0-101-generic/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice.ko firmware: updates/intel/ice/ddp/ice.pkg version: 2.3.15` Over time, you will observe eventually pods begin to fail all layer 3 communication. You will be able to inspect the cilium ip cache bpf map as improperly empty. This will be in contrast to what the API believes should be in the ebpf map. Cilium will log that it is appropriate regenerating the ipcache map frequently, but this is not correct. `time=2026-03-23T20:48:00.47345889Z level=debug source=/go/src/github.com/cilium/cilium/pkg/k8s/watchers/pod.go:246 msg="Updated ipcache map entry on pod add" module=agent.controlplane.k8s-watcher k8sPodName=bpinske-debugging-churn-29571648-0-6c6vp k8sNamespace=pool podIP="" podIPs=[] hostIP=""` I am investigating further the exact contents of the BPF_MAP_UPDATE_ELEM syscall with strace to try and understand why or how this is being blackholed. Attached is some cilium debug information. I am specifically including the output of `cilium bpf endpoint list` and `cilium endpoint list` demonstrating the discprepancy and incorrectness of the bpf map state. [cilium-dbg-bpf-endpoint-list.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26522536/cilium-dbg-bpf-endpoint-list.md) [cilium-dbg-endpoint-list.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26522535/cilium-dbg-endpoint-list.md) ### Cilium Version 1.18.7, 1.19.2 ### Kernel Version 5.15.0-72-generic and 6.8.0-101-generic ### Kubernetes Version 1.34.4 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-debuginfo-20260406-184840.459+0000-UTC.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26522554/cilium-debuginfo-20260406-184840.459%2B0000-UTC.md) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [x] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: Gateway API L7LB north-south traffic still dropped on 1.19.4 when LB VIP is announced on a VLAN subinterface (not a bridge)
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue? - Related: #43819, #44187 (same north-south L7LB class). This adds a data point: the merged fixes #44658 / #45582 do **not** resolve it when the ingress device is a **VLAN subinterface** rather than a Linux bridge. ### What happened? External (north-south) TCP to a Gateway API L7 LoadBalancer VIP (an endpoint-less `type: LoadBalancer` Service flagged `[LoadBalancer, l7-load-balancer]`) is silently dropped before reaching Envoy, on **Cilium 1.19.4** — which contains both #44658 and #45582. The LB VIP is advertised via Cilium L2 announcements on a **VLAN subinterface** (`vsw0.4042@uplink0`, a Hetzner vSwitch VLAN), not a Linux bridge. `br_netfilter` is loaded and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1`. Observed on a request to the VIP from an external client and from a pod: - `cilium monitor -v` shows the redirect decision firing: `-> proxy port 19052 ... <client> -> <vip>:4318 tcp SYN` (this is new in 1.19.4; on 1.18.10 there was **no** datapath event at all — so #44658/#45582 did change behavior). - But the packet **never reaches the Envoy socket**: `tcpdump -i lo port 19052` shows zero traffic; no SYN-ACK egresses on any interface; the client times out. - `cilium monitor --type drop` shows nothing (drop is not in the BPF datapath). - Routing primitives are all correct: `ip rule` has `from all fwmark 0x200/0xf00 lookup 2004`, table `2004` has `local default dev lo`, Envoy is listening on `127.0.0.1:19052` (`SO_REUSEPORT`), `rp_filter=0`. - **Host-netns-originated** traffic to the same VIP works (socket-LB path). - Ruled out: host firewall (tested with it disabled), and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=0` (tested — no change). This looks like the `MARK_MAGIC_TO_PROXY` + punt-to-stack / TPROXY-in-PREROUTING path from #36383, where the second PREROUTING pass is skipped (so the TPROXY rule never delivers to the socket). #44658 adds a hairpin fallback **gated on the device being a bridge**; our ingress device is a VLAN subinterface, so that fallback appears not to engage, and #45582’s `ctx->mark` fix doesn’t help here either. ### Question for maintainers Should the #44658 hairpin / #45582 fix also cover **non-bridge** netdevs (e.g. VLAN subinterfaces) when `br_netfilter` + `bridge-nf-call-iptables=1` cause `ip_sabotage_in()` to skip the second PREROUTING pass? Is there a recommended config to force the hairpin path for L7LB on such devices? ### Cilium Version 1.19.4 (upgraded from 1.18.10; behavior changed but issue persists) ### Kernel Version 6.8.0-117-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ### Kubernetes Version v1.34 (k3s) ### Relevant config - `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, `l7Proxy: true`, `loadBalancer.l7.backend: envoy` - `l2announcements.enabled: true`; LB-IPAM VIP announced on a VLAN subinterface - Gateway API (native Cilium GatewayClass), TLS-terminating listeners on 443/4317/4318

signals.title: ClusterMesh: configurable minimum healthy local backends before `affinity: local` falls back to remote
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? With ClusterMesh global services and `service.cilium.io/affinity: "local"`, the fallback to remote backends is **all-or-nothing**: remote backends are used only when there are **zero** active local backends. From [`pkg/clustermesh/selectbackends.go:73-77`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/pkg/clustermesh/selectbackends.go#L73-L77): ```go case annotation.ServiceAffinityLocal: // Always include the local backends even if they are unhealthy and // only include (healthy) remote ones if there are no healthy local backends. useLocal = true useRemote = localActiveBackends == 0 && remoteBackends > 0 ``` This causes a thundering-herd / cascading failure during local scale-up: - **Setup:** 3 clusters in ClusterMesh, a global service `svc1` with `service.cilium.io/global: "true"` and `service.cilium.io/affinity: "local"`, 30 replicas of the backend per cluster at steady state. - We scale the backend from **0 → 30** in a cluster. The instant the **first** local pod becomes Ready, `localActiveBackends` goes `0 → 1`, so `useRemote` flips to `false` and **all healthy remote backends in the other two clusters are dropped**. - That single local pod now receives 100% of the cluster's traffic, gets overloaded, and dies — while ~58 healthy remote backends sit idle. - `localActiveBackends` drops back to `0` → remote re-enabled → the next local pod becomes Ready → remote dropped again → it is hammered again. The result is flapping and cascading pod failures until enough local capacity comes up all at once. There is currently no way to express "prefer local, but keep using remote backends until the local cluster has enough Ready capacity." The fallback threshold is hardcoded to zero. ### Describe the feature you'd like A way to make the `affinity: local` → remote fallback trigger on a **configurable minimum number of healthy local backends**, rather than only at zero. Proposed: a new per-service annotation, e.g. `service.cilium.io/affinity-min-local-backends: "<N>"` (strawman name), with a default of `1` to preserve today's behavior exactly. Two possible semantics (happy to discuss which is preferable): - **(A) Graceful spill (preferred):** while `localActiveBackends < N`, include remote backends *in addition to* local ones, so traffic is shared across clusters until local capacity is sufficient; once `localActiveBackends >= N`, use local only. This keeps the small local pool from being overwhelmed during ramp-up without blackholing the local pods that are already up. - **(B) Threshold fallback:** while `localActiveBackends < N`, route to remote only; switch to local-only at `>= N`. Open design questions: - Hysteresis around the threshold to avoid flapping right at the boundary. - Whether the same knob should symmetrically apply to `affinity: remote`. This is a narrower, more tractable slice of the richer-affinity ask in #29200 (closed/stale), and is distinct from the `affinity: "none"` bug in #46623. ### Notify relevant community channels @cilium/sig-clustermesh (owns `pkg/clustermesh`) and @cilium/sig-lb (owns `pkg/loadbalancer`); the annotation lives under `pkg/annotation` (@cilium/sig-k8s). ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution The core change is localized to the `ServiceAffinityLocal` branch in [`pkg/clustermesh/selectbackends.go`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/pkg/clustermesh/selectbackends.go#L73-L77). For semantics (A): ```go case annotation.ServiceAffinityLocal: useLocal = true // minLocalBackends defaults to 1 → identical to the current `== 0` behavior. useRemote = localActiveBackends < minLocalBackends && remoteBackends > 0 ``` `minLocalBackends` would be parsed from the new annotation in `pkg/annotation` (alongside `GetAnnotationServiceAffinity`). With the default of `1`, `localActiveBackends < 1` is equivalent to `localActiveBackends == 0` for the non-negative integer count, so the change is **fully backward-compatible**. `localActiveBackends` already counts only `BackendStateActive` local backends, which is the desired "Ready local capacity" signal.

signals.title: v1.19.3: WireGuard handshakes never complete on any node pair (tunnel/geneve + DSR), all cross-node pod traffic dead, on Oracle Linux only.
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? After upgrading to Cilium 1.19.3, all cross-node pod-to-pod connectivity is dead cluster-wide. The root symptom is that the WireGuard handshake never completes between *any* pair of nodes, in *either* direction. Every node reports, for every one of its 5 peers: ``` latest handshake: 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z transfer: 0 B received, 9836672 B sent ``` ``` 96: cilium_wg0: <POINTOPOINT,NOARP,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1300 ... RX: bytes packets errors dropped missed mcast 0 0 0 0 0 0 TX: bytes packets errors dropped carrier collsns 44358560 299720 0 2162782 0 0 ``` `cilium-dbg status` shows host connectivity is healthy while the encrypted overlay is completely dead: ``` Cluster health: 1/6 reachable (2026-07-28T13:02:11Z) cl-13-kubesi-worker-0: Host connectivity to 10.47.2.203: ICMP to stack: OK, RTT=297.168µs HTTP to agent: OK, RTT=961.602µs Endpoint connectivity to 10.42.2.197: ICMP to stack: Connection timed out HTTP to agent: Get "http://10.42.2.197:4240/hello": context deadline exceeded ``` With `echo module wireguard +p > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` on `controlplane-1`: (pattern repeats like this, no 'receiving' alike messages) ``` [427001.163104] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 11) [427001.163232] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Sending handshake initiation to peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) [427001.175653] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Sending handshake initiation to peer 1 (10.47.2.194:51871) [427004.235068] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 5 (10.47.3.11:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 2) [427006.284042] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 12) [427006.284054] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 2 (10.47.2.203:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 18) [427023.178883] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 2 (10.47.2.203:51871) did not complete after 20 attempts, giving up ``` I ran claude on this, here's the output: ## What I have already ruled out I did a fairly deep investigation before filing. The following are all **not** the cause: | Hypothesis | Evidence against | |---|---| | **Public key mismatch** | All 6 nodes' live interface keys match their `CiliumNode` `network.cilium.io/wg-pub-key` annotations exactly, and match the corresponding peer entries on other nodes | | **Wrong endpoints / allowed-ips** | Each peer has `endpoint: <nodeIP>:51871` and `allowed ips: <nodeIP>/32`, which is correct for tunnel mode (geneve-encapsulated outer packet) | | **Clock skew (TAI64N replay rejection)** | Node clocks agree within ~1.8s | | **Cilium BPF dropping packets** | `cilium-dbg monitor --type drop -v` shows nothing during reproduction; `cilium-dbg bpf metrics list` shows no drop reasons other than an unrelated `Unsupported L3 protocol` on IPv6 RouterSolicitation | | **Issue #46100 (fragment tracking)** | No `DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND` counter present on any node. Handshake initiations are 148 B, far below any MTU | | **Host firewall** | `iptables` OUTPUT rule `ACCEPT all -- 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.0/8 state NEW` covers node-to-node traffic (2.7M packets); no DROP rule counter increments during reproduction | | **rp_filter** | `IPReversePathFilter` stays at 0 across bursts (note: `enp1s0/rp_filter=1`, `all=0`, so effective strict — but it is demonstrably not dropping these) | | **Network fabric blocking UDP** | Disproved by measurement — see below | | **Socket not bound / socket drops** | `ss -unlp` shows `UNCONN 0.0.0.0:51871`; `/proc/net/udp` shows `drops=0` for that socket | ### Measurement showing UDP does traverse the fabric Sending synthetic UDP bursts node-to-node (`worker-0` → `worker-1`, both `10.47.2.0/24`): - Receiver NIC counter (`/proc/net/dev`, counted before BPF): `5,603,727 → 5,608,812` = **+5,085 for 5,000 datagrams sent**. Packets reach the wire and the NIC. - Receiver netfilter INPUT hook, diffing `iptables-save -c` around a 3,000-packet burst to port 51871: ``` DELTA=3371 filter [27595:1956942] -A INPUT -m comment --comment "cilium-feeder: CILIUM_INPUT" -j CILIUM_INPUT DELTA=3361 filter [9070529:4141298931] -A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL DELTA=3371 raw -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_raw DELTA=3371 mangle -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_mangle DELTA=2999 nat -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_nat ``` So synthetic UDP to 51871 is routed for local delivery and passes netfilter without being dropped. Node-to-node TCP and ICMP work normally throughout (confirmed by Cilium's own health prober, RTT ~0.3–1 ms). So: the path carries UDP, the keys are right, nothing visibly drops the packets, and yet no peer ever answers a handshake initiation. ### How can we reproduce the issue? Surprisingly: this setup **works** on Ubuntu-based setup, I found this to be broken only on Oracle Linux 1. RKE2 cluster, 6 nodes (3 control-plane, 3 workers), Oracle Linux 9.8 / UEK kernel. 2. Cilium 1.19.3 with the config below: `routing-mode: tunnel` + `tunnel-protocol: geneve`, `encryption.type=wireguard` (nodeEncryption disabled), kube-proxy replacement with `loadBalancer.mode=dsr` and `dsrDispatch=geneve`. 3. Physical NIC MTU 9000 (happens on different clusters with "regular" MTU of 1500 too) , Cilium `MTU: 1380` (yields `cilium_wg0` MTU 1300). 4. Observe `cilium-dbg debuginfo | grep -A5 'peer:'`, all peers show `latest handshake: 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` and `0 B received`. Relevant Helm values: ```yaml MTU: 1380 encryption: enabled: true type: wireguard tunnelProtocol: geneve kubeProxyReplacement: true loadBalancer: algorithm: maglev dsrDispatch: geneve mode: dsr bpf: masquerade: true hostLegacyRouting: false localRedirectPolicies: enabled: true pmtuDiscovery: enabled: true # or false, doesn't matter, both yield same outcome ``` ### Cilium Version `Cilium: Ok 1.19.3 (v1.19.3-f5eb641b)` ### Kernel Version ``` 5.15.0-322.203.3.4.el9uek.x86_64 ``` ### Kubernetes Version ``` 1.35 (v1.35.5+rke2r2) [linux/amd64] ``` ### Regression Yes. This cluster worked before the upgrade to Cilium 1.19 (version: v1.18.3). Connectivity broke at the upgrade. WireGuard has never completed a single handshake in the current agents' lifetime (4d+ uptime, `latest handshake: never`). ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell KubeProxyReplacement: True [enp1s0 10.47.3.11 fe80::21a:4aff:fe16:1c4 10.47.17.1 (Direct Routing)] CNI Chaining: portmap Cilium: Ok 1.19.3 (v1.19.3-f5eb641b) IPAM: IPv4: 14/126 allocated from 10.42.0.128/25 Routing: Network: Tunnel [geneve] Host: BPF Attach Mode: Legacy TC Device Mode: veth Masquerading: BPF [enp1s0] 10.42.0.128/25 [IPv4: Enabled, IPv6: Disabled] Controller Status: 86/86 healthy Encryption: Wireguard [NodeEncryption: Disabled, cilium_wg0 (Pubkey: 7we7...fjk8=, Port: 51871, Peers: 5)] Cluster health: 1/6 reachable Modules Health: Stopped(23) Degraded(0) OK(113) ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: With Gateway API, the 3-way handshake fails when Envoy and the Backend Pod are running on the same Node.
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/42325 ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? It is structured as follows. When the backend Pod and the assigned Envoy are on the same Node, the 3-way handshake between the Envoy and the Pod fails. As a result, the Envoy returns a 503 error to the client. When the assigned Envoy and the backend Pod are on different Nodes, it works normally. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client 192.168.0.10] -->|to 10.1.1.66| B[bgp router] B --> C[Envoy] B --> D[Envoy] B --> E[Envoy] subgraph cilium_host 10.0.1.12 C -->|Failed| F[Backend 10.0.1.41] end subgraph cilium_host 10.0.2.183 D -->|Success| F end subgraph cilium_host 10.0.0.179 E -->|Success| F end ``` ### Failed Pattern: [Client] -> [Backend Pod Running Node] - hubble log ``` 10.0.1.12:54518 (ingress) -> default/whoami-5996d44689-hhnw4:80 (ID:47342) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN) 10.0.1.12:54518 (host) <- default/whoami-5996d44689-hhnw4:80 (ID:47342) to-stack FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN, ACK) 192.168.0.10:40936 (ingress) -> default/cilium-gateway-default-gateway:80 (world) http-request FORWARDED (HTTP/1.1 GET http://whoami.example.test/) 192.168.0.10:40936 (ingress) <- default/cilium-gateway-default-gateway:80 (world) http-response FORWARDED (HTTP/1.1 503 4999ms (GET http://whoami.example.test/)) 10.0.1.12:54518 (host) <- default/whoami-5996d44689-hhnw4:80 (ID:47342) to-stack FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN, ACK) 10.0.1.12:54518 (host) -> default/whoami-5996d44689-hhnw4:80 (ID:47342) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: RST) ``` - tcpdump (With a debug container attached to the envoy pod) ``` 03:36:39.863257 eth0 In IP 192.168.0.10.52434 signals.title: policy_log field not populated for host firewall policies (CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy with nodeSelector)
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version 1.19.1 ### What happened? We use the `log` field on our network policies so that matching flows get tagged with a name we can search for in our flow logs. On a normal `CiliumNetworkPolicy` that selects pods this works great, the `policy_log` field shows up with our value. However this does not seem to work on host Policies set via `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy` with a `nodeSelector` instead of an endpoint selector. Traffic clearly matches them (the rules are enforced, and I can see the flow with `hubble observe`), but `policy_log` is always empty for those. Same for `ingress_allowed_by`, nothing gets attached. So the `log` field basically does nothing on host firewall policies. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Enable host firewall and hubble (`hostFirewall.enabled=true`, hubble + flow export on). 2. Apply a host policy with a log value: ```yaml apiVersion: cilium.io/v2 kind: CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy metadata: name: allow-ssh spec: nodeSelector: matchLabels: example.io/host-fw: "true" ingress: - toPorts: - ports: - protocol: TCP port: "22" log: value: allow-ssh ``` 3. `hubble observe -t policy-verdict --node <node> -o json` — the flow is there, verdict is FORWARDED, but `policy_log` comes back empty. 4. For comparison, a regular `CiliumNetworkPolicy` that selects a pod with the same `log.value` does populate `policy_log`. ### Cilium Version 1.19.1 ### Kernel Version 6.8.0-134-generic (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS) ### Kubernetes Version RKE2 v1.32.13+rke2r1 ### Regression Not a regression as far as I know, I think it never worked for host policies. ### Anything else? I found #33870, which looks like the same underlying gap (policy verdict correlation not covering host firewall policies). It was closed as not planned, but from what i undestand this is seems to be the issue. The `log` field is exactly what we'd want for auditing what actually reaches the nodes (SSH, kube-api, ICMP, etc), and right now there's no way to get that for host policies at all. We'd really like to see this work for `nodeSelector` policies too, not just pod-selected ones. ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: cilium-agent <-> cilium-envoy livelock on cilium.NetworkPolicy xDS after upgrading to 1.20.0 — sustained 85-100% CPU on every node, no CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumEnvoyConfig present
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues. Closest match I found is #43770 ("CI: Conformance L7-only (ci-l7): connection disruption during agent restart") — same `agent.controlplane.envoy-proxy` / `cilium.NetworkPolicy` xDS code path and affects v1.19/v1.20, but that one is a restart-time race that self-resolves within ~3-4 minutes via the policy-restore fallback timeout. What we hit did not involve an agent restart and did not self-resolve (ran at 85-100% CPU for 40+ minutes until we manually restarted the pods). Flagging both here in case they share a root cause, but filing separately since the trigger and recovery behavior differ. ## Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ## What happened? About 13 hours after a clean upgrade from 1.19.6 to 1.20.0 (Helm chart_version bumped in lockstep with the image tag, DaemonSet rolled 6/6 nodes with no errors, `cilium connectivity test` passed clean before and after with no new failures), all 3 worker nodes in a 6-node cluster (3 control-plane, 3 workers) climbed to 85-100% CPU, sustained, with no change in actual traffic pattern. Root cause turned out to be cilium-agent and its embedded cilium-envoy stuck in an unbounded xDS request/response loop over the `type.googleapis.com/cilium.NetworkPolicy` resource: - cilium-agent logs showed continuous `OnStreamRequest`/`OnStreamResponse` pairs (module=`agent.controlplane.envoy-proxy`), with `xdsNonce` incrementing forever and never converging — e.g. nonce went from 6421447 to 6421520 (73 increments) within about 180ms in one sample window. A 10-second log capture on one node's agent contained 44,950 `OnStream*` log lines (~4,495/sec). - The corresponding cilium-envoy container logged `Ignoring unwatched type URL type.googleapis.com/cilium.NetworkPolicy` (grpc_mux_impl.cc:396) continuously, every 3-5ms, forever. - Two xDS version hashes were involved throughout and never matched: the agent kept serving `xdsVersion=f494f7846` while envoy kept requesting against `xdsVersion=5dc77ff454`. - This happened with **zero** `CiliumNetworkPolicy`, `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy`, `NetworkPolicy`, or `CiliumEnvoyConfig` objects present anywhere in the cluster. The only thing enabling L7/Envoy involvement is `hubble.metrics` including `httpV2` (L7 HTTP visibility) — that config predates this upgrade and was untouched by it. - Control-plane nodes (which don't run this cilium-agent DaemonSet workload the same way / weren't under similar churn) were unaffected the entire time — CPU stayed at 8-15%. The timing correlated with — but as far as we can tell wasn't directly caused by — an unrelated pod churn event on the cluster (a healthcheck controller's periodic DaemonSet/Deployment/DNS check pods being created and torn down on a ~20-30 minute cycle). Our working theory is that this churn triggered enough endpoint/policy recomputation to tip an already-fragile 1.20.0 xDS reconciliation into the livelock, but we don't have a minimal repro yet. **Expected behavior**: cilium-agent and cilium-envoy's xDS NetworkPolicy stream should converge to a stable version and go quiet absent further policy/endpoint changes, as it did under 1.19.6. ## How can we reproduce the issue? We don't have a minimal repro yet — this took ~13 hours of real cluster uptime plus what we believe was a churn trigger to manifest, and it did not reproduce immediately after the initial upgrade/rollout verification. Our environment, for context: 1. 6-node bare-metal/VM cluster (3 control-plane, 3 workers), Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-136-generic. 2. Cilium installed via Helm (`chart_ref: cilium/cilium`, `chart_version` == app version, always in lockstep). 3. Relevant Helm values: `ipv6.enabled: true` / `ipv4.enabled: false` (IPv6-only), `routingMode: native`, `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, `hubble.enabled: true` with `hubble.metrics.enabled` including `httpV2`, `bgpControlPlane.enabled: true`. 4. No `CiliumNetworkPolicy`/`CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy`/`NetworkPolicy`/`CiliumEnvoyConfig` objects defined anywhere in the cluster. 5. Upgraded `cilium_version` 1.19.6 -> 1.20.0 via `helm upgrade`. Rollout itself was clean (verified via `cilium status`, `hubble status`, and `cilium connectivity test` pre/post). 6. ~13 hours later, worker-node CPU began climbing, fully saturating over roughly 10-15 minutes, coincident with unrelated pod churn elsewhere in the cluster. **Workaround**: a full restart of cilium-agent + cilium-envoy (we used a node reboot, since `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` intentionally leaves DaemonSet pods running and a plain pod delete would likely work too but we didn't test that specifically) immediately cleared the loop — CPU dropped from 85-100% to 9-11% within about a minute, and the xDS request rate returned to a handful of requests per 15 seconds (normal baseline) on all three affected nodes. This is a workaround, not a fix — the underlying condition is presumably still reachable and could recur on the next churn event. ## Cilium Version ``` Client: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 ``` Image: `quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.20.0@sha256:383968cd5e8873f7976fa76aa6196045643558f4cc9518a207b9335cb24a0e93` ## Kernel Version ``` Linux node-0 6.8.0-136-generic #136-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jul 1 21:53:05 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux ``` ## Kubernetes Version ``` Client Version: v1.36.3 Server Version: v1.36.3 ``` ## Regression Yes. Cluster ran on 1.19.6 for an extended period without this issue. Only started after upgrading to 1.20.0, and only manifested ~13 hours post-upgrade rather than immediately. ## Sysdump Not captured at the time — we didn't realize the significance until CPU was already saturated and prioritized restoring service. Happy to attempt to reproduce and capture one in a maintenance window if that would help, since the fix-by-reboot workaround means we can safely force the condition again if there's a reliable way to trigger the churn that seems to precede it. ## Relevant log output cilium-agent (module=agent.controlplane.envoy-proxy), representative sample — this pattern repeated continuously for 40+ minutes until the pod was restarted: ``` time=2026-07-30T19:25:09.729497532Z level=info msg=OnStreamResponse module=agent.controlplane.envoy-proxy xdsStreamID=1 xdsVersion=f494f7846 xdsNonce=6421520 xdsResourceNames=[] ``` cilium-envoy, same time window: ``` [2026-07-30 19:26:16.806][7][warning][config] [external/envoy/source/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/grpc_mux_impl.cc:396] Ignoring unwatched type URL type.googleapis.com/cilium.NetworkPolicy [2026-07-30 19:26:16.813][7][warning][config] [external/envoy/source/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/grpc_mux_impl.cc:396] Ignoring unwatched type URL type.googleapis.com/cilium.NetworkPolicy [2026-07-30 19:26:16.819][7][warning][config] [external/envoy/source/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/grpc_mux_impl.cc:396] Ignoring unwatched type URL type.googleapis.com/cilium.NetworkPolicy ``` (repeating every 3-5ms, indefinitely) `kubectl top nodes` before / after the workaround reboot (worker nodes only): ``` node-0 997m (99%) -> 106m (10%) node-1 999m (99%) -> 112m (11%) node-2 1702m (85%) -> 82m (4%) ``` ## Anything else? Possibly related: #43770 discusses a chicken-and-egg fence between `CiliumEnvoyConfig` initialization and the Envoy xDS server waiting on initial policy computation during endpoint regeneration, in the same `agent.controlplane.envoy-proxy` / `cilium.NetworkPolicy` code path. We don't use `CiliumEnvoyConfig` at all, so if these share a root cause it's likely in the more general Envoy NetworkPolicy xDS reconciliation logic rather than the CiliumEnvoyConfig-specific fence path described there. - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the Users doc - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: loader: investigate lost BPF complexity coverage
signals.text: When porting variables from macros to dynamic config variables, we've lost coverage in complexity tests. An example is the `EVENTS_MAP_RATE_LIMIT`: * in v1.19, we were running complexity tests with `-DEVENTS_MAP_RATE_LIMIT=1000` * in v1.20 we ported it to a `CONFIG` variable, without adding it to the test permutations (or removing it afterwards to stay in the limit, haven't double checked). This means the respective codepath (i.e., `if (CONFIG(events_map_rate_limit) > 0)`) is never verified. ([occurred](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/actions/runs/30582390390/job/91102334498) on [this backport](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47620)) This means we're potentially hitting complexity issues we're not aware of in main.

signals.title: L7 CiliumNetworkPolicy: ingress proxy upstream leg never completes — pod's SYN-ACK reaches the veth but not the host stack (1.20.0, kernel 6.1, tunnel/vxlan)
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ## What happened? When any L7 `CiliumNetworkPolicy` is attached to an endpoint, the **ingress proxy's upstream leg (Envoy → backend pod) never completes its TCP handshake**, and the affected Service becomes unreachable for as long as the policy exists. Removing the policy restores it instantly. The downstream leg works correctly: eBPF marks the packet, `iptables` TPROXY redirects it, Envoy's transparent socket accepts it, Envoy parses the HTTP request, and Hubble emits an `http-request FORWARDED` flow. Only the leg **after** that fails. ``` client ──► eBPF mark ──► iptables TPROXY ──► Envoy transparent socket ──► HTTP parse ──► Hubble L7 flow OK OK OK 36 pkts OK cx_total 9 OK OK │ Envoy ──► backend pod ◄──────────────────────┘ FAIL: SYN sent, pod replies SYN-ACK on the lxc veth, but the SYN-ACK never reaches the host stack. RST after ~2s. 26/26 = 100%. ``` `envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_connect_timeout{envoy_cluster_name="ingress-cluster"}` equals `envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_total` — **every** upstream connection times out. Critically, `cilium-dbg monitor --type drop` reports **zero drops**, so the packet is lost silently somewhere between the veth ingress and the host network stack. This looks closely related to how the ingress proxy's upstream connection is classified in conntrack — see **Possible root cause** below. ### tcpdump — the failing leg, with a working control in the same capture Captured with `tcpdump -i any -e -n` in the host netns. The full pcap is attached. **Control — before the policy is applied.** Same source IP, same pod, same veth: ``` 12:55:09.853371 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 Out 10.42.0.213.55556 > 10.42.0.204.9187: Flags [S] 12:55:09.853388 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 In 10.42.0.204.9187 > 10.42.0.213.55556: Flags [S.] 12:55:09.853414 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 Out 10.42.0.213.55556 > 10.42.0.204.9187: Flags [.], ack 1 ^ the ACK goes out, i.e. the host stack received the SYN-ACK. Connection proceeds normally. ``` **Downstream leg with the policy applied — works.** This is the kubelet HTTP readiness probe being TPROXY-redirected into Envoy: ``` 12:55:24.853830 cilium_host Out 10.42.0.213.49598 > 10.42.0.204.9187: Flags [S] 12:55:24.853849 lo In 10.42.0.204.9187 > 10.42.0.213.49598: Flags [S.] ^ Envoy's transparent socket answers on lo, spoofing the pod address 12:55:24.853936 cilium_host Out 10.42.0.213.49598 > 10.42.0.204.9187: Flags [P.], length 110 ^ GET /metrics HTTP/1.1 12:55:25.854421 cilium_host Out ... Flags [F.] (kubelet timeoutSeconds: 1 gives up) ``` **Upstream leg with the policy applied — fails.** This is Envoy connecting to the backend pod: ``` 12:55:24.854560 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 Out 10.42.0.213.49608 > 10.42.0.204.9187: Flags [S] 12:55:24.854572 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 In 10.42.0.204.9187 > 10.42.0.213.49608: Flags [S.] ^ the pod answers correctly, the SYN-ACK reaches the veth ... ^ ... and is never seen again. It appears on NEITHER cilium_host NOR lo. 12:55:25.879008 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 Out 10.42.0.213.49608 > ...: Flags [S] (retransmit) 12:55:25.879027 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 In 10.42.0.204.9187 > ...: Flags [S.] 12:55:27.891029 lxcc4bd6dbfdc72 In 10.42.0.204.9187 > ...: Flags [S.] 12:55:27.891099 cilium_host Out 10.42.0.213.49608 > ...: Flags [R] (RST, ~3s in) ``` The contrast between the control and the failing leg is the core of this report: **the identical path (same veth, same source IP, same destination pod) works without the policy and drops the SYN-ACK with it.** ### conntrack — only `ProxyRedirect` entries never see return traffic ``` $ cilium-dbg bpf ct list global | grep '10.42.0.204:9187' # with the L7 policy attached: TCP IN 10.42.0.213:49598 -> 10.42.0.204:9187 RxFlagsSeen=0x1b TxFlagsSeen=0x00 \ Flags=0x0051 [ RxClosing SeenNonSyn ProxyRedirect ] TCP IN 10.42.0.213:53672 -> 10.42.0.204:9187 RxFlagsSeen=0x1b TxFlagsSeen=0x00 \ Flags=0x0051 [ RxClosing SeenNonSyn ProxyRedirect ] TCP IN 10.42.0.213:39982 -> 10.42.0.204:9187 RxFlagsSeen=0x1b TxFlagsSeen=0x00 \ Flags=0x0051 [ RxClosing SeenNonSyn ProxyRedirect ] # same pod, before the policy was attached: TCP IN 10.42.0.213:47702 -> 10.42.0.204:9187 RxFlagsSeen=0x1f TxFlagsSeen=0x1a \ Flags=0x0013 [ RxClosing TxClosing SeenNonSyn ] TCP IN 10.42.0.213:60840 -> 10.42.0.204:9187 RxFlagsSeen=0x1f TxFlagsSeen=0x1a \ Flags=0x0013 [ RxClosing TxClosing SeenNonSyn ] ``` Every entry carrying `ProxyRedirect` has `TxFlagsSeen=0x00` — no return traffic ever observed. Every entry without it has `TxFlagsSeen=0x1a`. No exceptions. ### Envoy metrics (read from the Prometheus endpoint on `:9964`) ``` envoy_listener_downstream_cx_total{envoy_listener_address="127.0.0.1_10488"} 9 envoy_http_downstream_cx_total{envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="proxy"} 9 envoy_http_downstream_rq_total{envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="proxy"} 9 envoy_http_downstream_rq_rx_reset{envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="proxy"} 9 envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_total{envoy_cluster_name="ingress-cluster"} 26 envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_connect_fail{envoy_cluster_name="ingress-cluster"} 26 envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_connect_timeout{envoy_cluster_name="ingress-cluster"} 26 ``` Envoy accepts and parses fine; 100% of upstream connections time out. The `rx_reset` count reflects the kubelet probe (`timeoutSeconds: 1`) resetting before Envoy's upstream timeout elapses — with a client that waits longer, Envoy returns `503 upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers ... connection timeout`. ### Hubble confirms the request reaches L7 ``` $ hubble observe --protocol http Aug 5 12:56:10.856: 10.42.0.213:41478 (host) -> forge/postgres-exporter-...:9187 (ID:54041) \ http-request FORWARDED (HTTP/1.1 GET http://10.42.0.204:9187/metrics) ``` Because no response is ever produced, `hubble_http_requests_total` stays at zero series — the httpV2 handler only emits on responses. This makes the failure additionally hard to spot from metrics alone. ### Ruled out by measurement | Hypothesis | How it was checked | Result | |---|---|---| | Envoy's listening socket is not `IP_TRANSPARENT` | `ss -lnptOe --inet-sockopt` in the host netns | **transparent is set** on all 4 worker sockets (`fwmark:0xa00`) | | Proxy port mismatch / stale redirect | `cilium-dbg status --all-redirects`, `iptables-save -t mangle`, Envoy listener dump | all `10488`, exactly one redirect | | Missing kernel modules | `/proc/modules` | `xt_TPROXY`, `xt_socket`, `nf_tproxy_ipv4/v6`, `nf_socket_ipv4/v6`, `nf_defrag_ipv4/v6` all loaded | | Envoy / iptables in different netns | `readlink /proc/self/ns/net` | identical (`net:[4026531840]`) | | Host firewall (ufw) eating proxy traffic | `CILIUM_INPUT` vs `INPUT` policy DROP deltas in a window where TPROXY fired 36 pkts | `CILIUM_INPUT` ACCEPT +43, `INPUT` DROP +3 (background rate). Not ufw. | | Policy enforcement / default-deny | `enableDefaultDeny: {ingress: false, egress: false}` visibility-only policy | **identical failure** | | eBPF explicitly dropping | `cilium-dbg monitor --type drop` | 0 drops | | Kernel rejecting the connection | `nstat`: `ListenDrops`, `ListenOverflows`, `TCPReqQFullDrop`, `TcpAttemptFails` | all unchanged during failure | | xDS delivery | agent + Envoy logs | `lds: add/update listener 'cilium-http-ingress:10488'` on every attach | | Standalone vs embedded Envoy | tested both | fails in both (embedded surfaces it as a 503 because clients wait long enough) | | `rp_filter` | `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/rp_filter` | all 0 | | Leftover CNI from a previous mesh (Linkerd) | `/etc/cni/net.d`, iptables nat, CRDs | clean | ## Cilium Version ``` Client: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 ``` cilium-envoy: `quay.io/cilium/cilium-envoy:v1.37.5-1782911245-7cffc778c923f68a77954a53b1a98d6b5353f004` (`sha256:583057dd4f7d54cd41efff3c413aa0b148ac201f522e2c3336851fa89c78b039`) Note: Kubernetes 1.36 is only supported by Cilium 1.20, so downgrading to test an earlier minor is not an option here. ## Kernel Version ``` Linux 6.1.0-50-amd64 x86_64 GNU/Linux (Debian 12) ``` ## Kubernetes Version ``` Client Version: v1.36.2+k3s1 Server Version: v1.36.2+k3s1 ``` Single node, 4 vCPU / 31 GiB. ## Relevant configuration ``` kube-proxy-replacement true routing-mode tunnel tunnel-protocol vxlan datapath-mode veth ipam cluster-pool identity-allocation-mode crd enable-l7-proxy true external-envoy-proxy true # standalone cilium-envoy DaemonSet (also reproduced with embedded) envoy-xds-mode ads bpf-lb-sock false enable-ipv4-masquerade true enable-bpf-masquerade (unset) # also reproduced with this set to true enable-host-legacy-routing (unset) enable-endpoint-routes (unset) devices (auto) # also reproduced pinned to a single device enable-ipv6 false ``` `cilium-dbg status`: ``` KubeProxyReplacement: True [enp3s0 192.168.219.100 (Direct Routing), tailscale0 100.118.42.102] Routing: Network: Tunnel [vxlan] Host: Legacy Masquerading: IPTables [IPv4: Enabled, IPv6: Disabled] Proxy Status: OK, ip 10.42.0.213, 1 redirects active on ports 10000-20000, Envoy: external Controller Status: 283/283 healthy ``` ## How can we reproduce the issue? **Pick a target that actually receives HTTP traffic.** This matters — I initially used a Service whose readinessProbe was `tcpSocket`, saw `downstream_cx_total = 0`, and wrongly concluded that Envoy was never receiving connections. It was simply never being sent any HTTP. Here I use a `postgres-exporter` whose readinessProbe is `httpGet /metrics` and which is scraped by Prometheus, so requests flow continuously. **1. Baseline** ```bash kubectl -n forge run probe --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl:8.5.0 -- \ -sS --max-time 8 -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code} connect %{time_connect}s\n" \ http://postgres-exporter:9187/metrics # HTTP 200 connect 0.000613s ``` **2. Attach a visibility-only L7 policy** (no enforcement — `enableDefaultDeny` disabled in both directions, so this changes nothing except turning on L7 parsing) ```yaml apiVersion: cilium.io/v2 kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy metadata: name: l7-vis-postgres-exporter namespace: forge spec: endpointSelector: matchLabels: app: postgres-exporter enableDefaultDeny: ingress: false egress: false ingress: - fromEntities: - all toPorts: - ports: - port: "9187" protocol: TCP rules: http: - {} ``` **3. Observe** ```bash # the redirect and listener come up cleanly kubectl -n kube-system exec ds/cilium -c cilium-agent -- cilium-dbg status --all-redirects | grep -A2 'Proxy Port' # cilium-http-ingress 856:ingress:TCP:9187: 10488 kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/cilium-envoy | grep lds # lds: add/update listener 'cilium-http-ingress:10488' # Envoy accepts and parses, but every upstream connection times out curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9964/metrics | grep -E 'ingress-cluster.*(connect_fail|connect_timeout|cx_total)' # conntrack: ProxyRedirect entries never see return traffic kubectl -n kube-system exec ds/cilium -c cilium-agent -- cilium-dbg bpf ct list global | grep ProxyRedirect # no eBPF drops are reported kubectl -n kube-system exec ds/cilium -c cilium-agent -- cilium-dbg monitor --type drop ``` The Service is unreachable for as long as the policy exists; the pod goes `0/1` because its HTTP readiness probe now fails. **4. Remove the policy — recovery is immediate** (`HTTP 200`, ~0.6 ms). Reproduced 100% of the time across many attempts, on `admin-front:3000` and `postgres-exporter:9187`, with standalone and embedded Envoy, with and without `bpf.masquerade`, with `devices` auto-detected and pinned. ### Capturing the packet trace The node's `ss` was too old for `--inet-sockopt` (iproute2 6.1.0; the option needs 6.4+), so I ran the socket and packet inspection from a netshoot pod sharing the host netns: ```bash kubectl -n kube-system run netshoot-diag --image=nicolaka/netshoot --restart=Never \ --overrides='{"spec":{"hostNetwork":true,"hostPID":true, "containers":[{"name":"netshoot","image":"nicolaka/netshoot","command":["sleep","3600"], "securityContext":{"privileged":true}}]}}' kubectl -n kube-system exec netshoot-diag -- \ tcpdump -i any -e -n "tcp port 9187 or tcp portrange 10000-20000" -w /tmp/l7.pcap ``` One note for anyone else chasing this: `tcpdump port 10488` will **always** be empty. TPROXY hands the packet to the socket without rewriting the destination, so no packet ever carries `127.0.0.1:10488` as an address. I lost time on this assumption. ## Possible root cause I have not confirmed this in the datapath code, and I would appreciate a maintainer pointing me at the right place — I am happy to write the fix once the code path is identified. **The ingress proxy's upstream connection is 5-tuple-shaped like the downstream connection it is serving, and the return traffic appears to be classified as proxy-redirect traffic a second time.** Because `cilium-envoy` runs in the host netns, its upstream connection to the backend uses the `cilium_host` address as source. In this cluster that is `10.42.0.213`, which is also the source address of the host-originated traffic being proxied. So both legs look like: ``` downstream (client → proxy): 10.42.0.213:49598 → 10.42.0.204:9187 upstream (proxy → backend): 10.42.0.213:49608 → 10.42.0.204:9187 ``` They differ only in source port. Both create `TCP IN` conntrack entries toward the same `dst:dport`, and in the captured state **both** carry the `ProxyRedirect` flag while neither records any return traffic (`TxFlagsSeen=0x00`). My working hypothesis is that when the pod's SYN-ACK enters `from-container` on the lxc veth, the reverse-direction CT lookup matches an entry marked `ProxyRedirect` and the packet is steered toward the proxy instead of being delivered to the host stack where Envoy's client socket is waiting. That would explain every observation at once: - the SYN-ACK is visible on the veth but on neither `cilium_host` nor `lo` - no drop is reported (the packet is redirected, not dropped) - kernel TCP rejection counters stay flat (it is non-delivery, not refusal) - the downstream leg is unaffected (it is the direction the redirect is meant for) - removing the policy — and with it the `ProxyRedirect` classification — fixes it instantly If that is right, the fix would live in how Envoy's upstream socket mark (`MARK_MAGIC_PROXY_INGRESS`, `0xa00`, which `ss` confirms is set on the listening socket) is expected to exempt the connection from re-redirection, and why that exemption is not taking effect on the return path here. It is possible this only manifests in the specific combination below, which is why I have listed it explicitly: - `routing-mode: tunnel` (vxlan) **combined with** `KubeProxyReplacement` reporting `Direct Routing` - `enable-bpf-masquerade` unset, so `Routing: Host: Legacy` and `Masquerading: IPTables` — an unusual pairing with `kube-proxy-replacement: true`. I also reproduced it with `bpf.masquerade: true` (`Host: BPF`), so this does not appear to be the trigger, but the two paths differ enough to be worth checking. - `bpf-lb-sock: false` Happy to run any additional instrumentation on this cluster — it is a lab node and I can attach the policy and break it at will. ## Anything else? **Attachments** (I will attach these to the issue directly): - `cilium-sysdump-during-failure.zip` — sysdump taken **while the policy was attached and failing**, so it contains the failing CT entries and Envoy stats - `l7-upstream-leg-failure.pcap` — the full `tcpdump -i any -e` capture containing both the working control and the failing upstream leg **Impact.** L7 features are unusable on this cluster: no L7 policy, and no `hubble_http_*` metrics, since requests never produce responses. Attaching a policy to get metrics takes the Service down, and the only status code it would ever record is `503`. L3/L4 policy, flow visibility, `hubble_flows_processed_total`, `hubble_tcp_flags_total` and the service map all work normally.

signals.title: Pre-flight ahead of 1.20 upgrade doesn't drop CiliumNodeConfig v2alpha1 CRD
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? [Asked first on Slack](https://cilium.slack.com/archives/C1MATJ5U5/p1785758062847279), but another person confirmed experiencing this too. One of the upgrade notes mentioned the upgrade of `CiliumNodeConfig` from `v2alpha1` to `v2`. I checked beforehand: ```sh $ kubectl get ciliumnodeconfigs.v2alpha1.cilium.io --all-namespaces Warning: cilium.io/v2alpha1 CiliumNodeConfig will be deprecated in cilium v1.16; use cilium.io/v2 CiliumNodeConfig No resources found ``` I then installed the preflight check: ```sh $ helm install cilium-preflight oci://quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium --version 1.20.0 \ --namespace kube-system \ --set preflight.enabled=true \ --set agent=false \ --set operator.enabled=false Pulled: quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium:1.20.0 Digest: sha256:8009baed89d99fd84f7ee5cfdbf3a1fae8153452132549833956b6aca8b9d738 NAME: cilium-preflight LAST DEPLOYED: Mon Aug 3 13:32:10 2026 NAMESPACE: kube-system STATUS: deployed REVISION: 1 DESCRIPTION: Install complete TEST SUITE: None NOTES: You have successfully ran the preflight check. Now make sure to check the number of READY pods is the same as the number of running cilium pods. Then make sure the cilium preflight deployment is also marked READY 1/1. If you have an issues please refer to the CNP Validation section in the upgrade guide. Your release version is 1.20.0. For any further help, visit https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.20/gettinghelp ``` Now, I merged my upgrade PR so Flux rolled out the upgrade from 1.19.6 to 1.20.0. However, the operator pods end up in `CrashLoopBackOff` with this error around `CiliumNodeConfig`: ``` time=2026-08-03T11:52:00.976886093Z level=error msg="Start hook failed" module=operator function="apis.createCRDs.func1 (.../k8s/apis/cell.go:64)" error="unable to create CRDs: Unable to create custom resource definition: CustomResourceDefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io \"ciliumnodeconfigs.cilium.io\" is invalid: status.storedVersions[0]: Invalid value: \"v2alpha1\": missing from spec.versions; v2alpha1 was previously a storage version, and must remain in spec.versions until a storage migration ensures no data remains persisted in v2alpha1 and removes v2alpha1 from status.storedVersions" ``` Now the CNP validator didn't return anything: ``` $ kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/cilium-pre-flight-check -c cnp-validator --previous Error from server (BadRequest): previous terminated container "cnp-validator" in pod "cilium-pre-flight-check-f65fdb894-qthmk" not found ``` The `v2alpha1` storage version CRD hasn't been dropped during the upgrade. ### How can we reproduce the issue? I ran an upgrade of Cilium v1.19.6 to v1.20.0 on my homelab cluster. I'm not sure if this is reproducible for everyone though. ### Cilium Version Upgrade from Cilium v1.19.6 to v1.20.0. ### Kernel Version 6.18.39-talos arm64 on Raspberri Pi CM4 ### Kubernetes Version v1.36.3 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-20260805-163930.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30748735/cilium-sysdump-20260805-163930.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: node-init startup script fails on GKE >= 1.36.2-gke.2064000: GKE-containerd probe no longer matches node image
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.0 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? After GKE auto-upgraded cluster nodes from `1.36.2-gke.1498000` to `1.36.2-gke.2064000` (Rapid channel, 2026-R32 rollout), every `cilium-node-init` pod crash-looped and no cilium agent ever started, causing a cluster-wide outage. Node-init logs: ``` [pod/cilium-node-init-mpzc5/node-init] Device "cbr0" does not exist. [pod/cilium-node-init-mpzc5/node-init] bash: line 121: kubelet: command not found [pod/cilium-node-init-mpzc5/node-init] !!! startup-script failed! exit code '127' ``` ### Root cause The startup script's GKE-containerd probe ```bash if [[ -f "${GKE_KUBERNETES_BIN_DIR}/gke" ]] && [[ $(grep -cF -- '--container-runtime-endpoint' "${KUBELET_DEFAULTS_FILE}") == "1" ]]; then ``` no longer matches on the `gke.2064000` node image. Kubelet still *runs with* the `--container-runtime-endpoint="unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock"` flag (visible in the node journal), so GKE apparently assembles kubelet flags elsewhere now and `/etc/default/kubelet` no longer contains it (or the `gke` marker file is gone — node shell access is restricted on GKE, so I could not determine which of the two conditions fails). The script then falls into the generic branch, which runs: ```bash K8S_VERSION=$(kubelet --version) ``` `kubelet` is not in the PATH of the startup-script container (it lives at `/home/kubernetes/bin/kubelet` on the host), so this exits 127. With `set -o errexit` the script dies before writing `/tmp/cilium-bootstrap.d/cilium-bootstrap-time`, so the agent's `wait-for-node-init` init container blocks forever. Result: no CNI, `cilium-agent-not-ready` taint never cleared, nothing schedules — a full cluster deadlock that also takes down konnectivity (no kubectl logs/exec) and any admission webhook with `failurePolicy: Fail`. Note the fallback branch is unreachable by design: it invokes a bare `kubelet`, which the container never has in PATH, so *any* probe miss necessarily produces this outcome. The identical script is still on `main`: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/install/kubernetes/cilium/files/nodeinit/startup.bash ### Environment - cilium 1.19.6 via Helm chart, `nodeinit.enabled=true`, `reconfigureKubelet=true`, `removeCbrBridge=true` - GKE Rapid channel, regional cluster - Broken node image: `gke-1362-gke2064000-cos-129-19506-299-3-c-pre` (kernel 6.12.94, containerd 2.2.3) - Working node image: `gke-1362-gke1498000-cos-129-19506-224-80-c-pre` (kernel 6.12.90, containerd 2.2.3) - Downgrade to the working version is not possible — GKE removed it from valid versions ### Suggested fix - Make the probe robust, e.g. key on `/home/kubernetes/bin/kubelet` existing (GKE-specific path) instead of / in addition to the current markers; and/or - Use an absolute path (`/home/kubernetes/bin/kubelet --version`) or a PATH-safe guard in the fallback branch so a probe miss degrades gracefully instead of deadlocking the cluster. ### Workaround we are using Restore both markers before the probe via the chart's `nodeinit.startup.preScript` hook: ```bash touch /home/kubernetes/bin/gke if ! grep -qF -- '--container-runtime-endpoint' /etc/default/kubelet 2>/dev/null; then echo 'KUBELET_OPTS="${KUBELET_OPTS:-} --container-runtime-endpoint=unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock"' >> /etc/default/kubelet fi ``` This makes the probe pass on both the old and the new node image and preserves the kubelet wrapper. Disabling `reconfigureKubelet` also avoids the crash but loses the wrapper (reboot persistence for the containerd `conf_template` workaround), so we avoided that. ### How can we reproduce the issue (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. GKE Rapid cluster on `1.36.2-gke.2064000` (or let nodes auto-upgrade to it) 2. Install cilium Helm chart with `nodeinit.enabled=true`, `nodeinit.reconfigureKubelet=true` 3. Watch `cilium-node-init` pods crash-loop with exit 127; `cilium` agent pods stuck at `Init:4/7` (`wait-for-node-init`)
